# facil.io patch series

Applies to facil.io `5128747363055201d3ecf0e29bf0a961703c9fa0` (the `deps/facil.io`
submodule), in the order listed in `series`. `apply.sh <dest>` copies
`deps/facil.io/lib` to `<dest>/lib` and applies the series; the submodule itself
is never modified. Each patch applies with `patch -p1` or `git apply` on top of
the previous ones.

The library is built with the flat command from the plan (all of
`lib/facil/**/*.c` except `legacy/`, `-DHAVE_OPENSSL -DFIO_TLS_FOUND`). Patch 09
adds a zlib dependency (`-lz`) for WebSocket permessage-deflate.

`test/patches/run.sh` applies the series, builds it and runs the correctness
suites named below.

| # | Patch | What it changes | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `tmpfile-unlink` | `fio_tmpfile()` unlinks the file right after `mkstemp`, so spooled request bodies leave nothing in the temp directory. | `features` (no `facil_io_tmpfile_*` left after an upload over 8 KiB) |
| 02 | `exact-timers` | kqueue: the poll timeout keeps its sub-second part (no busy poll while a short timer is pending), a timer's due time counts from the real clock instead of the cycle start, and the poll arms a no-leeway one-shot kqueue timer for the first due timer. epoll is unchanged. | `timers` |
| 03 | `gather-write-path` | Packets carry inline framing (up to 20 bytes before and 8 after the buffer). `fio_flush` sends the run of buffer packets at the head of the queue in one `writev` on plain sockets; the slow-reader guard trips when such a `writev` is only partly taken while 1,024 packets and 4 MiB are still queued (a lagging reader of many small packets, such as a WebSocket subscriber, is left to its protocol). New: `fio_write_framed` (no-copy write with framing and a flush mode), `fio_flush_or_schedule`, `fio_pending_bytes`, `fio_drain_notify`, `http_send_body_nocopy` (head and caller's body in one `writev`, `dealloc` called once), `http1_stream_begin/end/end_now` (unknown-length response on a keep-alive connection). kqueue events carry the uuid, so an event that outlives its connection is ignored; a re-arm happens only while the uuid is still open; only one of two racing closers clears the fd. | `write`, `large`, `mixed` |
| 04 | `close-race-guards` | `fio_read` holds the socket lock across the read hook, and `fio_force_close` re-checks the uuid under the lock before calling the hook's `before_close`, so a close on one thread cannot free TLS state another thread is using. Poll-side forced closes skip connections that are already closed. | `tls` (abrupt closes, 1,000 mid-download aborts), `ws` (churn) |
| 05 | `tls-layer` | OpenSSL layer rewrite: plaintext is encrypted a chunk at a time with one socket write per chunk, idle connections hold no input buffer, a handshake waiting on the peer asks for no write event (no spin on silent or half-open connections), SNI with one context per name, password-protected keys, an EC key instead of RSA for the generated certificate, and new configuration calls `fio_tls_configure` (versions, ciphers, flags), `fio_tls_cert_set_pem` (hot reload), `fio_tls_trust_pem`, `fio_tls_on_context`, `fio_tls_ctx`. | `tls` (safety and configuration) |
| 06 | `http-robustness` | Request-head deadline (`http1_header_timeout_set`, default 30 s, answers 408), blank-line flood limit, correct error statuses (400, 408, 413, 414, 431) with `connection: close` and a lingering drain so the client reads the reply, early 413 on a declared oversize body, reading stops while replies are queued (slow readers no longer grow memory), static files: single-range parsing with 416, quoted ETags, `If-None-Match` lists, `If-Range`, HEAD without body (also on `http_send_body` and `http_send_body_nocopy`), OPTIONS, `last-modified` on `http_sendfile`, error pages served without recursion; `sendfile` stops at a truncated file; idle-timeout review walks the connection table in one pass per second; `fio_accept_batch_set`; parser rejects negative or non-numeric `content-length`, `content-length` with `transfer-encoding`, and negative chunk sizes. | `robust` |
| 07 | `fd-capacity` | The connection table is sized from `FIO_CAPA` (environment) when set, the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` is only ever raised and the hard limit is left alone. | `mixed` (start-up), memory measured in the M10 scoreboard |
| 08 | `request-body` | Request bodies over the read buffer are received straight into their final place, chosen per request when the head is complete (`http1_body.h`): in the read buffer, one exact-size `malloc` block, caller memory, a streaming callback with back-pressure, or a temp file. `Expect: 100-continue` is answered. Stricter framing: chunk-size lines, a coding list that does not end in `chunked`, repeated `transfer-encoding`. Without `http1_body_configure` the stock `h->body` behaviour is kept. | `upload`, `mixed` |
| 09 | `websockets` | WebSocket fixes and features: frame parser hardening, UTF-8 validation (close 1007), close codes (`websocket_close2`), 1 MiB per-thread read buffer for large frames, permessage-deflate without context takeover (`websocket_deflate_set`), slow-subscriber limits and policies, broadcast frames shared across subscribers. Pub/sub delivers in publishing order per channel (`fio_subscription_inline`). Write path: `fio_writev_now`, `fio_pending_drop`, the `lazy` flag on `fio_write2`, packets from the system allocator, `ENOBUFS` treated as retry. | `ws`, `features`, `mixed` |
| 10 | `websocket-controls` | Per-connection WebSocket controls: `websocket_close3` (close code plus a reason of up to 123 bytes), `websocket_max_msg_size_set`, `websocket_utf8_check_set`, `websocket_read_pause` (stop reading from the peer until restarted; frames already read are still delivered). A message that arrives as one whole frame is now held to the size limit too (1009); before, only fragmented and partly read frames were. | `ws`; Facil's `test/websockets.jl` |
| 11 | `tls-write-buffer` | TLS write path: plaintext is encrypted up to 1 MiB per socket write (`FIO_TLS_WRITE_CHUNK`, was 128 KiB) into a per-thread spare buffer that a connection borrows and returns once the socket took everything (no allocation or page faults per chunk); a connection whose socket fills drops to 64 KiB chunks and doubles back after each write taken whole, so a slow reader holds little encrypted data. New hooks `fio_flush_elsewhere` / `fio_flush_wake`: when set, `fio_flush` on a connection with read/write hooks (TLS) from a thread the hook names defers the flush to the reactor and wakes it; Facil sets them so TLS is only ever flushed on the reactor thread. | `tls`; Facil's `test/tls.jl` |
| 12 | `websocket-perf` | WebSocket unmasking 16 bytes at a time (vector extension, scalar fallback). `websocket_deflate_codec_set`: whole-message compress/decompress callbacks that replace zlib for permessage-deflate (Facil plugs in zlib-ng to compress, with a sync flush, and libdeflate to decompress); incoming messages get the removed `00 00 ff ff` plus an empty final block before the whole-buffer decompression. | `ws`; Facil's `test/websockets.jl` |
| 13 | `kqueue-rearm-batch` | kqueue: a connection's read re-arm (after its `on_data` found the socket drained) is queued and handed to the kernel in the next poll's `kevent` call instead of costing its own syscall; re-arms made while a thread is inside that call go out at once, and queued ones whose connection closed are dropped. WebSocket `on_data` stops after a read that emptied the socket (`WS_SKIP_DRAINED_READ`, now 1) instead of trying one more read. WebSocket echo, 10 connections: +19% at 64 B, +7% at 16 KB. | all suites; Facil's full test suite |
| 14 | `epoll-uuid-events` | epoll: events carry the uuid they were armed for (`epoll_data.u64`) instead of the fd, and one whose connection closed (uuid no longer current, or not open) is ignored, as on kqueue since 03; before, an event for a closed fd whose number a new connection had taken was delivered to, and could force-close, the new connection. kqueue is unchanged. | `fdreuse` (keepers survive connection churn with descriptor reuse; run on Linux by `scripts/linux_smoke.sh` and the CI Linux job, also passes on kqueue) |
| 15 | `http1-shared-read-buffer` | HTTP/1.1 connections no longer carry an 8 KiB read buffer each: reads land in one buffer per reactor thread, and only bytes left unparsed when `on_data` returns (a partial head, pipelined requests, a paused request) are moved to a block of the connection's own, freed once they are consumed. The protocol object drops from 8,544 to 352 bytes. | `robust`, `upload`, `write`, `mixed`; Facil's `test/conn_scale.jl` |
| 16 | `close-mark-race` | The close marker is set only after the uuid is re-checked, under the socket lock, to still name an open connection (`fio_close`, `fio_force_close`, poll-side forced closes on EOF or error). Before, a closer that checked the uuid and lost the CPU while that connection closed and a new one took its fd set the marker on the new connection, which was then closed early (when it had queued data) or never read again (`deferred_on_data` skips connections marked closed). The same holds for the `scheduled` flag `deferred_on_data` releases before `on_data` and takes back after it to decide on the read re-arm: a task finishing for a connection that had just closed took the flag of the fd's next connection, whose own task then skipped its re-arm and was never read again. Both take real parallelism to hit: 1 in 5 runs of `fdreuse` with orderly closes at 8 reactor threads lost a keeper. When the socket lock is busy (a flush in progress, possibly on the calling thread), `fio_close` retries the mark from a task instead of waiting. | `fdreuse` (orderly-close churn mode, 4 and 8 threads) |
| 17 | `reactor-thread-wake` | Thread pool: an idle reactor thread sleeps on a condition variable that each task push signals (up to 100 ms, `FIO_DEFER_IDLE_WAIT_MS`), instead of facil's `nanosleep` back-off that grows to milliseconds, and the task-queue locks spin briefly before yielding. kqueue with more than one thread: read re-arms go to the kernel at once from the thread that finished with the connection, under its socket lock (13's batching stays for one thread), registrations use `EV_DISPATCH` instead of `EV_ONESHOT`, and a thread out of tasks polls without blocking while the last poll filled its event array. Timer tasks in flight keep the poll timeout at 1 ms until they re-queue their timer. At 8 reactor threads: CPU-bound handler 112k → 124k req/s, tiny JSON 165k → 170k (scoreboard rows 1, 3). | `fdreuse` (20 runs each, both churn modes, 4 and 8 threads), all suites; Facil's full test suite |
| 18 | `kqueue-per-thread` | kqueue with more than one thread: each pool thread owns a kqueue, and fd `n` belongs to kqueue `n % threads`. Only the owner thread waits on that kqueue, changes the fd's registrations and calls `close()` on it; another thread (a pool thread, a Julia thread) posts the change or close to the owner's inbox and wakes it with an `EVFILT_USER` trigger. Events still go to the shared task queue; an owner's own re-arms ride its next wait's change list, an EOF close happens on the owner as it polls, and a pool thread busy with the shared queue polls its kqueue without blocking every 16 tasks. Idle pool threads sleep on their own kqueue instead of 17's condition variable; a task push wakes one. Descriptors registered before the pool starts (listeners, the wake pipe) move to their owner's kqueue; after the pool joins, inboxes are drained and shutdown polls every kqueue from one thread. Reason: on macOS, `close()` on a socket whose knote sits in a kqueue other threads are waiting on can block in the kernel forever (unkillable process); a standalone repro with one kqueue per thread (`kqclose4`) ran clean where the shared kqueue hung. One thread, epoll and poll are unchanged. | `fdreuse` (20 runs each, both churn modes, 4 and 8 threads), all suites; Facil's full test suite |
| 19 | `slow-reader-would-block` | The slow-reader guard from 03 also trips when a gathered `writev` takes nothing (`EAGAIN`) while 1,024 packets and 4 MiB are queued, not only when it takes part. On Linux, loopback sends complete inside the sender's call, so a never-reading client fills its socket during the first writes and every later flush would block outright; the guard never saw a partial write there. | `robust` (flood: 30 never-reading clients dropped, on Linux in the CI Linux job) |
| 20 | `http-conformance` | The status line carries the number the response was given for every status from 100 to 999: `http_status_reason_set` installs a reason phrase per status (Facil installs HttpTypes' canonical phrases), and a status without one is written as `NNN Unknown` instead of `500 Internal Server Error`; `http_status2str` follows. A request line with a space after the target (`GET /a b HTTP/1.1`) is a parse error (400). `http_finish` adds no `content-length` to 1xx, 204 and 304 responses. Static files: a percent-encoded NUL in the path makes `http_sendfile2` return -2 and the public-folder lookup answer 400; `http_settings_s.public_folder_flags` (the former `reserved1`, so the struct layout is unchanged) takes `HTTP_PUBLIC_DENY_DOTFILES` (no path with a segment that starts with a dot) and `HTTP_PUBLIC_CONTAIN_SYMLINKS` (no file whose real path leaves the folder). | Facil's `test/conformance.jl`; `robust`, `features` |
| 21 | `websocket-shutdown` | `websocket_shutdown(uuid, close_others)`: from any thread, a WebSocket gets its `on_shutdown` callback and a 1001 close and is closed, as at reactor shutdown; another kind of connection is closed when `close_others` is set and left alone otherwise. Facil's shim uses it to close or drain one server. | Facil's `test/conformance.jl`, `test/websockets.jl`; `ws` |

Where two spike patches disagreed, the merge keeps:
- one write path, the gather-write path of 03; the two-buffer `fio_write2v_fn` of the
  no-copy and memory spikes and the WebSocket spike's own gather are not carried;
- the robustness spike's single-pass timeout review instead of the memory spike's
  batched review (both remove the per-connection review task);
- the upload spike's stricter parser where it overlaps the robustness spike's parser
  fixes, and the robustness spike's `http1_reject` (with lingering drain) for every
  rejected request, including those rejected by the body planner;
- the write spike's unconditional `on_ready` re-check when reading is throttled
  (it only attempts a flush, so it cannot spin).
